drivingQuestion: What counts as 'most of the ribs' in the mishna's ruling that an animal most of whose ribs were fractured is a tereifa?
outcomeNote: A mishna lemma answered directly by a tannaitic definition; no argument is joined in this unit.

segments.he: נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ רוֹב צַלְעוֹתֶיהָ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן רוֹב צְלָעוֹת – שֵׁשׁ מִכָּאן וְשֵׁשׁ מִכָּאן, אוֹ אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מִכָּאן וְאַחַת מִכָּאן.
segments.en: § The mishna states that if «most of» an animal’s «ribs were fractured,» it is a tereifa. «The Sages taught: These are most of the ribs: Six from here and six from there,» i.e., six on each side, «or eleven from here and one from there.» Twenty-two ribs are significant for matters of tereifot, eleven on each side. Twelve fractured ribs constitutes a majority.
